summary: camelot-ammv2-core exfiltrates installer secrets to webhook.site at install time
details: The package's preinstall/postinstall runs index.js which scrapes process.env for keys matching KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASS/PRIVATE/MNEMONIC/AWS/GITHUB/NPM/WALLET, reads ~/.npmrc and ~/.gitconfig, and enumerates ~/.ssh, ~/.foundry/keystores, ~/.config/hardhat, and ~/.config/gcloud. It also collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, cwd, and platform, then POSTs the collected data over HTTPS to a hardcoded webhook.site receiver at path /326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09. The file header carries a cover-story comment identifying itself as a @plumenetwork/nest-artifacts install shim while the package is published under the unrelated name camelot-ammv2-core, and the install script swallows errors (`node index.js || true`, try/catch) so installation never fails and the exfiltration remains silent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
